description:
In August 2002, UK mobile users could dial the number 2580, hold their phone up to a song playing nearby, and hang up. About fifteen seconds later, a text message arrived naming the track and artist.

The number 2580 was not arbitrary. It is the only four-digit sequence that runs in a straight line down a standard phone keypad, easy to dial without looking. There was no icon to tap and no screen to check. The whole interface was a phone call.

roughly the share of UK mobile users who could use the service at launch, on every network except one.

It was not free. Each successful identification cost 50 pence, charged straight to the caller's phone bill. There was no app to open, because there was no app store yet for one to live in.

The company survived on this alone for six lean years, until Apple's App Store launched in July 2008 and gave Shazam an actual app to put the same idea inside. Growth took off almost immediately after.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shazam_(music_app): confirms Shazam Entertainment was founded in 1999 by Chris Barton, Philip Inghelbrecht, Dhiraj Mukherjee and Avery Wang, and that its original UK-only service, launched in August 2002, let users dial 2580, hold their phone up to a song playing nearby, hang up, and receive a text message naming the track, years before smartphones or app stores existed.
- https://cdm.link/shazam-is-20-years-old-history-trivia-and-tips/: confirms the service launched in the UK in August 2002, that dialling 2580 and holding the phone to the music returned a text message naming the song about fifteen seconds later, that 2580 was chosen because it is the only four-digit sequence in a straight line on a phone keypad, that the service was available to about 95 percent of UK mobile users at launch, and that each successful identification cost 50 pence on the user's phone bill.
